complexity.notes: The inner repaint loop runs O(n) per level rise and there can be O(n) rises, giving O(n^2) worst case. An O(n) version exists that keeps the same two-pointer skeleton but ||accumulates the trapped water at each position as the pointer steps past it, using the running best level, instead of rewriting the whole window|| — that also drops the auxiliary array to O(1) space. Minor style points: `water = [0 for h in height]` ignores `h`, so `[0] * len(height)` is the idiomatic spelling, and `best = max(best, level)` makes the preceding `if level > best` condition the only place `best` matters, so the update could live inside that branch.
complexity.summary: Two pointers close in from both ends, tracking the highest water level seen so far; every time that level rises, the code repaints the whole active window with the new level, then finally sums the excess over each bar. The repaint-per-rise turns an otherwise linear scan into a quadratic one on inputs with many level increases (e.g. strictly increasing heights).
